sections.html:
Property records are not available online right now. The Clay County Clerk has digitized deed records back to the 1960s, but you need to call or visit the clerk's office in Henrietta. Ask for the record by owner name, legal description or instrument number.

Two limits apply. The clerk cannot give legal advice or services, and has no duty to search public records, citing Attorney General opinion WW-607. A title company or attorney does the searching.

The office is in the Courthouse Annex at 214 N. Main Street, Henrietta, TX 76365, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 548. The phone is (940) 538-4631 and the fax is (940) 264-4160. Hours are Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the annex closes from noon to 1:00 p.m. every day.

  • The office closes for major holidays.
  • It may close for court hearings, training or bad weather, so call before a long drive.
  • Historic Commissioners' Court record books from the 1870s have been restored and are kept in the clerk's office.

sections.h2: Photo ID to file a deed
sections.html:
Bring a government photo ID. Senate Bill 16, effective September 1, 2025, added Local Government Code 191.010(b). The clerk must require photo ID from whoever presents a document for the real property records, must copy it, and must reject the filing if the person refuses.

The law is a statewide deed fraud measure. It also tightens criminal penalties for real property theft and fraud, lets victims seek restitution and a no-fee judicial voiding of a fraudulent deed, and sets stronger standards for notaries. If you plan to mail a deed, ask the clerk how the ID rule applies to documents delivered by a title company.

The first page costs $25 in total, and each added page costs $4, under the fee schedule effective September 1, 2025. Other recording fees are below.

The $25 first-page figure is a $10 archive fee, a $5 recording fee and a $10 records management fee. Each name to be indexed beyond five adds $0.25.

sections.h2: Mistakes that add fees or get a deed refused
sections.html:
Format errors raise the price or stop the filing:

  • No grantee mailing address on a deed signed after December 31, 1981 brings a penalty equal to the greater of twice the filing fee or $25, on top of regular fees.
  • No clear heading at the top of the first page doubles the filing fee for that page.
  • Names not legibly typed or printed under each signature double the fee for that page.
  • Printed type must be no smaller than 8 point (Local Government Code 191.007).
  • The deed needs original signatures and a proper acknowledgment under Property Code 12.001(b).

Copies cost $1.00 per page, certification is $5.00 per document, and a notice of trustee sale carries a $2.00 fee. A returned check costs $30.

The county clerk acts as the county recorder, and deed records are filed in the county where the land lies. Instruments a clerk records include general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, deed of trust releases and powers of attorney. A commissioners court can also tell the clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs. Ask the Henrietta office whether that option is in place.

If an owner has died, a probate filing may be needed before the house can be sold. A base probate or guardianship filing is $360, and $418 when a citation is issued and posted by the sheriff. A will left for safekeeping with the clerk costs $16. The clerk also has a guardianship registration form and civil court cost instructions.

Ask the clerk or a Texas attorney which route fits a particular estate. County clerks cannot advise on that choice.

The district handles value and exemptions, not tax collection. It does not levy taxes, set rates or collect them, so call the proper tax office for amounts. Its site, claycad.org, carries forms, an interactive map, protest hearing information and an oil and gas FAQ.

  • Homestead exemption: you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1, and it must be your principal residence. The claim covers up to 20 acres of residential land.
  • Filing window: January 1 to April 30 of the tax year, with a late homestead claim allowed up to two years after taxes become delinquent.
  • Over 65: the claim can be filed up to one year after the 65th birthday, with proof of age.
  • Mobile homes can be set up as improvement-only accounts if you file a request for separate taxation with the title or a verified purchase contract.

The usual protest deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after notice is delivered when that is later. A protest letter need not be on an official form.

sections.h2: Clay County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Clay County is thinly settled: 10,764 people in the July 2025 estimate, up from 10,218 at the 2020 census, across 1,088.76 square miles. It has 5,247 housing units, and owners occupy 84.0% of 4,289 households. The median owner-occupied home value is $171,500 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $811. Only 8 building permits were issued in 2025.

With so few sales, a comparable house may be miles away. Ask a title company for recent recorded deed prices in your part of the county.

faqs.q: Are Clay County property records available online?
faqs.a: No. Deed records are digitized back to the 1960s, but property records are not online. Call (940) 538-4631 or visit the annex in Henrietta.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Clay County Clerk?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with the annex closed from noon to 1:00 p.m. daily. The office may close for hearings, training or bad weather.

faqs.q: Do I need a photo ID to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Local Government Code 191.010(b), added by Senate Bill 16 effective September 1, 2025, the clerk must require photo ID from the person presenting a real property document, copy it and reject the filing if the person refuses.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: The schedule effective September 1, 2025 lists $25 for the first page and $4 for each added page. Missing grantee addresses, a missing heading or unreadable printed names add penalties.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Clay County?
faqs.a: Not the appraisal district. Call the proper tax office for amounts. The appraisal district's site has a separate Pay Taxes Online link for that purpose.
